We report the detection of a P-bearing molecule, phosphorus nitride (PN), for the first time in an extragalactic environment, towards two giant molecular clouds (GMCs) of NGC 253.
We derived a low excitation temperature of $T_{\rm ex}$=(4.4$\pm$1.3) K towards the GMC with the brightest PN emission, which indicates that PN is sub-thermally excited.

A non-LTE analysis derives a column density consistent with the LTE values, and confirms that the PN transitions are sub-thermally excited in a gas with volume density of the order of 10$^4$ cm$^{-3}$.

The central molecular zone (CMZ) of NGC 253 is one of the most prolific extragalactic sources for detections of molecules, as shown by previous spectral surveys, which revealed a rich chemical composition (e.g. (cite: Martin2006; Aladro2015; Meier2015; Ando2017; Martin2021)). This fact makes NGC 253 an excellent target for the search of new molecular species in the extragalactic ISM.
